artifact_review:
The Router identified 'text_gibberish' (Severity 3), 'texture_anomaly' (Severity 2), and 'structural_collapse' of the spool hub (Severity 2). 
1. Text Gibberish: Confirmed by the Image Text Auditor (low confidence scores ~0.53-0.78, nonsensical output 'JAR Aie GAOG'). Severity 3 is appropriate as it breaks semantic realism.
2. Texture Anomaly: Confirmed by Perceptual Quality Auditor ('noise', 'slight'). Severity 2 is fair; the plastic lacks the crisp specular highlights of real injection-molded plastic.
3. Structural Collapse: The Router noted the right spool hub looks fused. Visually, the hub lacks an axle hole and distinct teeth, appearing as a solid white disc. This is a mechanical plausibility error. Severity 2 is conservative; I would rate it Severity 3 because it fundamentally misrepresents the function of the object part, even if the overall shape is preserved.
4. New Artifact: The topology mask shows a clean boundary, but visually, the bottom edge of the cassette casing blends slightly into the background noise, lacking a sharp occlusion boundary. This is a minor edge artifact (Severity 1).
alignment_reasoning: The image is strongly aligned with the class 'cassette' (Fine Grained Classifier Top-1: cassette, logit 7.81). It possesses the correct global geometry (rectangular prism, rounded corners, two spool holes, head window). However, it fails the semantic requirement for the label text (gibberish instead of track info) and has minor mechanical inaccuracies in the spool hubs and write-protect tab details. It is not a perfect representation due to these functional/semantic flaws.
artifact_reasoning: Significant artifacts are present. The most prominent is text gibberish on the label (Severity 3), confirmed by OCR failure. The plastic texture exhibits digital noise/lack of realistic specular highlights (Severity 2). The internal spool hubs lack mechanical detail (axle holes/teeth), appearing fused/solid (Severity 3, upgraded from Router's 2). These artifacts prevent the image from achieving high photorealism, placing it below the 'high' reference standard.
